_comment: The Grade 4 Computing standalone lesson build, described for ../../mathematics/lesson-app-tools and built by ../lesson-kit. Order here IS the lesson number. Fourteen lessons organised by the strands of Cambridge Primary Computing 0059 Stage 4 (39 objectives), NOT by the units of the Word-pack course under computing/grade-4/data, so progress is written under l01..l14 - see THE UNIT PROBLEM in wire-progress.py. objectiveFloors are recorded at the measured value after each build and may rise, not fall.
subject: computing
hubStrands: Following, editing and correcting algorithms with repeat and forever loops and count-controlled iteration; repetition for concise algorithms; comparing algorithms for a purpose; predicting looped algorithms; decomposition into sub-routines and following them; algorithms with different outputs for different inputs; algorithms that include repetition.

Comments on code and why they help; programs with repetition and iteration; the repeat command; different outputs from different inputs; planning objects with their inputs and outputs; testing a program part by part; programming a physical device from its input devices, with count-controlled and forever loops.

Paper databases against digital ones; the pros and cons of forms; data against information; sorting data ascending, descending and alphabetically; data types for a field; using a database to answer a question; data, records and fields.
Servers and clients; the World Wide Web against the internet; wi-fi against ethernet; what goes wrong when a network fails; where and why encryption is used; the Caesar and Pigpen ciphers.

Control systems; application and systems software; the data input devices record, including sensors and data loggers; the information output devices communicate; file sizes; computer scientists across industries; robots in delivery, transport and health care.
